clue.text: Volkswagen is on order for driver, say

blocks.note: the Golf is a Volkswagen car model
an order is a society or fraternity; in a down clue the car sits on top of it

explanation.surface: Someone has a new Volkswagen on order for their chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' looks like a motorist, but a driver is the long-distance golf club; 'say' flags that it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a particular kind of golf club, used for long shots off the tee, so it is an example.

clue.text: Occasionally Barry may host

indicators.note: something done only occasionally happens every other time, so only every second letter counts

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A man named Barry might sometimes throw a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' does double duty in the surface but the letters come from both words; 'host' here means a great multitude, not a party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large crowd or body of people, especially an armed company, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Agreement of terms for you and Aardman – Nick Park oddly overlooked

indicators.note: terms are ends or limits, so only the closing letter of each named word is wanted
the odd-numbered letters of the park word are ignored, i.e. removed from the jail word

blocks.note: end of you
end of the studio's name
nick is British slang for jail
the first and third letters of Park, the ones taken out

explanation.surface: A note on how you and the Aardman studio got on once Nick Park, its famous animator, was left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Park is not one name here: Nick is prison, and Park's odd letters P and R are struck from it to leave ISON. Aardman is the Bristol studio behind Wallace and Gromit.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in full accord, so the word is a synonym for harmony or concord.

clue.text: Party time for those who’ve been on white powder?

definitions.text: Party time for those who’ve been on white powder?

blocks.clueFragment: Party time for those who’ve been on white powder?
blocks.note: surface reading: the comedown celebration for people who have taken cocaine
setter's reading: powder snow, and the social hour after a day on the slopes

explanation.walkthrough: White powder suggests a drug, but powder is fresh snow; the party is the drinking and socialising that follows a day spent skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term names the evening socialising at a ski resort, held after skiers come off the slopes.

clue.text: A celebrant working in place of worship

indicators.note: something working is in operation and being reshaped, so the letters are put to use in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest is on duty at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle was the portable sanctuary of the Israelites and now names a chapel or meeting house for worship.

clue.text: Criminals regularly flood bogs on the outside

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second one of the word that follows
the marshes sit outside, wrapping round the letters taken before

blocks.note: fens are low marshy land
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Criminals routinely flood the toilets of a prison block.
explanation.walkthrough: Bogs is British slang for toilets, which suits the surface, but here it means marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: Felons are people convicted of serious crimes, so the plural noun is a direct synonym for lawbreakers.

clue.text: Handle cross from the right – then hit on the counter

indicators.note: reading from the right means starting at the end, so the word for cross runs backwards
counter suggests running against the normal direction, so the word for hit is read backwards

blocks.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
to bonk is to hit, informally

explanation.surface: Instructions for hitting something on a shop counter after handling a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed: the rood becomes DOOR, then the bonk becomes KNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: The round fitting turned to open a door is its handle, so the compound names a kind of handle.

clue.text: Lad eating unlimited lunch – keep children’s party favourite?

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the first and last letters go
the lad takes the trimmed meal inside himself as food

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written before its ends are trimmed
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A boy eats a bottomless lunch at a party, and the children want to keep the favourite toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlimited means stripped of its limits, i.e. its first and last letters, not all-you-can-eat. A keep is the stronghold tower of a medieval fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable play structure is a classic hire for children's birthdays; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Set includes finale from Freddie Mercury for example

indicators.note: the word for set holds the selected letter within it
a finale is the closing part, so only the final letter of the name is used

blocks.note: to set something in the ground is to plant it
last letter

explanation.surface: A concert set ends with a Freddie Mercury song.
explanation.walkthrough: Freddie Mercury steers the solver to Queen; Mercury alone is the smallest body orbiting the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is one of the eight bodies orbiting the Sun, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Risky moment to discard jack

indicators.note: discarding a card throws it away, so the named letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a jiffy is a moment
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A card player judges it dangerous to throw away a jack just now.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or uncertain, so something iffy carries a chance of going wrong.

clue.text: Instrument in crate partner opens

blocks.note: a squeeze is an informal word for a romantic partner; opens puts it first
a crate is a box

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is found inside a crate when someone's partner opens it.
explanation.walkthrough: Opens is positional: the partner word comes at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze-box is a colloquial name for an accordion or concertina, which is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Split’s extremely Croatian – filled with passion

indicators.note: at the extremes means at the two ends, so only the outer letters are kept
the outer letters are stuffed with the passion word in their middle

blocks.note: first and last letters
love is a passion

explanation.surface: The Croatian city of Split is full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is capitalised to look like the Croatian port; the definition is the verb's past participle, and the apostrophe-s reads as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloven is an old past participle of cleave, meaning divided, as in a cloven hoof.

clue.text: Somehow leave cult leader to try meat

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some undetermined way, so the letters come out in an unknown order
a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter

explanation.surface: Someone escaping a cult is advised to sample meat, perhaps after a vegan sect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a slice of meat, and one cut from a calf is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Small functions initially giving warm, intimate feeling

blocks.note: cosines are trigonometric functions
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
surface padding: it does no work in the wordplay

explanation.surface: Small social gatherings at the start create a warm, close atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Functions suggests parties, but it means the maths functions; the abbreviation for small goes at the end. Initially seems only to steer the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Coziness is the state of being snug and comfortable, a feeling of warmth and closeness among people.

clue.text: President I see hosting supporter’s meeting with starter for Manchester City

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the exclamation holds the next word
a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter of the city name is used

blocks.note: aha is an exclamation of sudden understanding
a bra is a supporting undergarment
first letter
Lincoln is an English cathedral city

explanation.surface: A club president meets a fan before a Manchester City match.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester City looks like the football club, but City is a separate piece: Lincoln, the cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the sixteenth leader of the United States, so the name fits the title directly.

clue.text: Skilfully hiding rising chaos in congress

indicators.note: the word for skilfully conceals the next word within itself
in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

blocks.note: ably means skilfully
a mess is chaos

explanation.surface: A politician deftly covers up growing disorder in a legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: A congress is a formal gathering of delegates, and an assembly is likewise a body met together to deliberate.

clue.text: See 15
Connected to writing an American volume on biggest part of Amtrak railway

indicators.note: the setter takes the capital initial as the most prominent bit of the rail company's name

blocks.note: the US spelling of the metric volume litre
first letter
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A US book about the greater part of the Amtrak network.
explanation.walkthrough: Amtrak is the US passenger rail operator, which keeps the American theme; the volume is measured, not bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes things concerning books, authors and the written word, so it relates to writing.

clue.text: See 8
Cuppa, no milk – son replaces last of hot water?

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter, the only one wanted here
one letter is swapped in where another stood

blocks.note: tea without milk is black tea
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
the final letter, which is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone takes their tea black and the son swaps in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot water seems to belong with the tea; hot only supplies its last letter, and water alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The inland sea between Europe and Asia is a body of water; the question mark shows it is one example.

clue.text: Retired doctor breaking into concrete storeroom

indicators.note: breaking into a place means getting inside it
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the whole construction is read backwards

blocks.note: concrete means actual or real
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A retired doctor breaks into a concrete storage room.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired looks like it describes the doctor, but it reverses the whole assembly once the doctor is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard for storing food, so it is a kind of storeroom.

clue.text: Gasp on getting into tub

indicators.note: something that gets into a tub ends up inside it

blocks.note: a bath is a tub
re means on or about

explanation.surface: Someone gasps when getting into a cold bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasp is a single sudden intake of air, the same as one quick inhalation.

clue.text: Writers describing record muscles

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to trace round it, so the pens go round the record

blocks.note: Bics are ballpoint pens, from the brand name
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Authors write about record-breaking muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: Writers suggests authors, but here they are pens.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps are the large muscles at the front of the upper arm; the word works as a plural here.

clue.text: I time chat about taking R and R whimsically

indicators.note: the phrase goes round and takes in the first single letter
done on a whim means done capriciously, so the letters are arranged at random

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone times a chat about rest and relaxation, R and R.
explanation.walkthrough: R and R looks like rest and recreation. The second R is the definition: reading, writing and 'rithmetic are the three Rs, and whimsically owns up to the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the traditional three Rs of basic schooling, one stands for 'rithmetic, the sums part of elementary education.

clue.text: Hence almost red raw

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word is cut short by its final letter

blocks.note: so means therefore, hence
taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Something is therefore nearly red raw.
explanation.walkthrough: Red raw is a familiar pairing, but red belongs to the wordplay and raw stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that is raw is tender and painful, which is what the four-letter adjective describes.

clue.text: Band remains supporting Oasis, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter is taken
in a down entry a support sits underneath, so the remains come below the letter from the band name

blocks.note: middle letter
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A rock group remains as the support act for Oasis.
explanation.walkthrough: Band and Oasis suggest pop music, but the band is a strip of cloth; supporting places the remains below the letter in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of fabric worn round the waist or over a shoulder, so it is a band.

clue.text: Broadcast of TV show, Porridge for instance

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a TV serial is a show told in episodes

explanation.surface: A rerun of the TV sitcom Porridge is broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge was a much-loved British prison sitcom, which makes the TV show look like the definition; here porridge is oat breakfast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is made from oats, a grain, and is a breakfast dish of that kind, so it is an example.

clue.text: Showing Europe’s upset about vote

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
the jumbled letters go round the voting mark

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
a cross marked on a ballot paper is a vote

explanation.surface: A vote reveals that Europe is unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is the act of revealing or displaying something, which is what a showing of it amounts to.
